# Reduce bullet speed of enemies

## Problem statement

Enemy projectiles currently travel at 100–220 px/s, which the operator finds
too fast to read and dodge, making combat feel unfair rather than skilful. The
request is to reduce the bullet speed of **all** enemies — including the
boss — by **50 %**, so the player has more reaction time while the rest of the
enemy tuning (fire cadence, patterns, lifetimes) stays as it is.

## Users

- **Player** — benefits from slower, more readable incoming fire and more
  space to dodge, without enemies becoming trivial.
- **Game designer / AI agent** — needs a single, unambiguous reduction applied
  consistently across the runtime CSV, the fallback defaults, and the entity
  fallback constants, so game, gyms and CSV-load-failure behaviour all agree.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want enemy bullets to move at half their current speed so
  that I can read and dodge patterns instead of being hit by projectiles I
  cannot react to.
- As a **player**, I want the boss's bullets reduced by the same 50 % as the
  regular enemies so the boss fight is consistently more readable.
- As a **developer**, I want the reduction applied to every source of enemy
  bullet speed (CSV, defaults, entity constants) so the tuning cannot drift
  between the game and the gyms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Runtime CSV halved.** Every `bulletSpeed` value in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` (the runtime source of truth) is exactly half
  its previous value: scout 180→**90**, diver 220→**110**, tank 150→**75**,
  phaser 180→**90**, swarm 180→**90**, boss 160→**80**, asteroid 100→**50**,
  harvester 100→**50**.
- [ ] **AC2 — Fallbacks and entity constants halved.** Every `bulletSpeed` in
  `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) is halved (scout
  200→**100**, diver 220→**110**, tank 150→**75**, phaser 180→**90**, swarm
  180→**90**, boss 160→**80**, asteroid 100→**50**, harvester 100→**50**), and
  the hard-coded entity fallback constants are halved: `SCOUT_BULLET_SPEED`
  200→**100**, `DIVER_BULLET_SPEED` 220→**110**, `TANK_BULLET_SPEED`
  150→**75**, `PHASER_BULLET_SPEED` 180→**90**, `SWARM_BULLET_SPEED`
  180→**90**, `BOSS_BULLET_SPEED` 160→**80**, and the `BaseEnemy` default
  fallback 200→**100**. The boss desperation multiplier continues to scale
  from the halved base.
- [ ] **AC3 — Testing / validation.** Existing expectations that pin the old
  values (e.g. `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts` scout 200) are updated, and a
  focused test asserts that each archetype's CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS`, and
  entity-constant `bulletSpeed` is exactly half the pre-change baseline, and
  that the player's `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` (350) and every enemy
  `bulletLifetime` are **unchanged**.
- [ ] **AC4 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries. Specifically, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (enemy
  bullet speeds) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the
  `bulletSpeed` config reference) state the new values, and note that effective
  range (`bulletSpeed × lifetime`) therefore also halves because lifetimes are
  unchanged.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new
  changes, including the difficulty-sequencer tests — the generated campaign
  must still satisfy its per-wave target difficulty after the `bulletSpeed`
  difficulty factor shifts.

## Constraints

- **Bullet speed only.** Enemy `bulletLifetime`, fire interval, shot pattern,
  burst count and shot probability are unchanged. Effective range
  (`bulletSpeed × lifetime`) consequently halves as a side effect, which is
  acceptable and expected.
- **Player weapons are out of scope.** `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` (350 px/s),
  player weapon lifetimes and AOE radii are unchanged (they were halved
  separately by AH-0MUU131PU006O7ZD).
- **No formula re-tuning (Q3-A).** `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed` (40–600) and the
  `enemyDifficulty` weights are unchanged. The resulting small drop in
  archetype difficulty scores is accepted; the campaign targets are not
  re-tuned.
- **Gym parity.** The gym enemy config sliders/overrides read the same values,
  so no divergent copy may be introduced; any enabled object runs one shared
  implementation (see `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1).
- **Surgical change.** Do not reconcile unrelated pre-existing divergence
  between CSV and `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` values (e.g. scout's CSV 180 vs
  default 200); each value is simply halved in place.

## Existing state

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` is the **runtime source of truth**: `configStore`
  boots from it (dev via `/api/csv/...`, production via the bundled `?raw`
  import). `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` in `src/core/configDefaults.ts` is only the
  CSV-load-failure fallback, and the per-entity constants
  (`SCOUT_BULLET_SPEED`, etc.) are only used when a config omits `bulletSpeed`.
  This means halving only the defaults would not change runtime gameplay.
- Current values (CSV / default / entity constant): scout 180 / 200 / 200,
  diver 220 / 220 / 220, tank 150 / 150 / 150, phaser 180 / 180 / 180,
  swarm 180 / 180 / 180, boss 160 / 160 / 160, asteroid 100 / 100 / —,
  harvester 100 / 100 / —. `BaseEnemy` also has a bare `?? 200` fallback.
- `bulletSpeed` is a weighted factor in `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`
  (weight 5 of 116, normalised over 40–600 px/s), so lowering it lowers
  archetype difficulty scores and can nudge curve-generated campaign waves.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 documents enemy speeds using the
  **default** values (200/220/150/180/180/160), which already diverge from the
  CSV for scout; this brief treats the CSV as the runtime baseline.

## Desired change

Halve the enemy `bulletSpeed` in all three sources of truth so the game, the
gyms, and the CSV-load-failure fallback all ship the reduced speed, then
update the pinned tests and the documentation. Player projectile speed and all
enemy lifetimes remain unchanged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Halve the `bulletSpeed` column for all 8 rows.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — Halve `bulletSpeed` in every `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` entry.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — `SCOUT_BULLET_SPEED` 200→100.
- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — `DIVER_BULLET_SPEED` 220→110.
- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — `TANK_BULLET_SPEED` 150→75.
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — `PHASER_BULLET_SPEED` 180→90.
- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — `SWARM_BULLET_SPEED` 180→90.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — `BOSS_BULLET_SPEED` 160→80.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — default `_bulletSpeed` fallback 200→100.
- `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts` — Update the pinned scout-200 assertion.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` (and/or a focused new test) — Assert the exact 50 % reduction across CSV/defaults/constants and that player speed and enemy lifetimes are unchanged.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 — Update the enemy bullet-speed baseline prose.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Update the `bulletSpeed` config reference.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts` / campaign tests — Re-verify if generated wave composition shifts.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Difficulty-score shift (medium).** Halving `bulletSpeed` lowers each
  firing archetype's difficulty score by roughly 0.5–1 point (weight 5/116).
  Curve-generated waves (L4–L5 and the dynamic opening waves) could shift
  composition near their targets. Mitigation: run the difficulty-sequencer
  tests; if a target is no longer met, record it rather than silently
  re-tuning (Q3-A explicitly accepts the shift).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Tempting adjacent changes — re-tuning
  `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed`, reconciling the scout CSV/default divergence,
  or touching enemy lifetimes — are deliberately **out of scope**. Record any
  such opportunity as a linked work item, not as extra scope here.
- **Assumption.** "All enemies" includes the two non-firing rows
  (asteroid, harvester) for table uniformity, even though their speed is inert
  (Q1-A).
- **Assumption.** The gym editor slider range (40–600) and
  `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed` are unchanged; only the shipped values change.
- **Assumption.** Existing custom ("Save As") enemy configs persisted in
  localStorage are out of scope — only shipped archetypes are halved.

## Related work

- AH-0MUU131PU006O7ZD — Reduce the starting range of all weapons by 50%
  (closest precedent; halved **player** weapon range and left enemy lifetimes
  unchanged).
- AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB — Speed power up should increase all speeds (player-only
  P5 boost; does not affect enemy bullets).
- AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 — Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around
  the screen (introduced the `bulletSpeed × lifetime` range model).
- AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K — Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy
  is to survive (the `enemyDifficulty` metric whose `bulletSpeed` factor
  shifts).
- AH-0MULW9HNC001GVCY — Tune enemy balance: reduce scout durability and tank
  firing (prior enemy balance tuning).
- AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT — enemy-configs.csv consistency with
  `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` (precedent for keeping CSV and defaults aligned).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which enemy archetypes are in scope?**
  Answer (operator): **All 8 rows in `enemy-configs.csv`** (scout, diver, tank,
  phaser, swarm, boss, asteroid, harvester), for a uniform table; the two
  non-firing rows are inert. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Which sources of truth get halved?**
  Answer (operator): **CSV + `configDefaults` + hard-coded entity constants**
  are all kept consistent. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Difficulty calibration (`bulletSpeed` feeds `enemyDifficulty`).**
  Answer (operator): **Accept the small score shift**; verify the generated
  campaign still meets its targets and run the full suite; do not rescale
  `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed` or exclude the factor. Source: interactive reply.

**Recommended options** (stated during the interview): Q1-A, Q2-A, Q3-A —
each chosen by the operator.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUJRGVD4004Z9EI** – Danger detection helper and constants (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: boss, bullet, enemies, including, reduce (+1 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: boss, bullet, enemies, including, reduce (+1 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: boss, bullet, enemies, including, speed


## Plan

Planning review completed 2026-10-06 (auto-complete path: effort Small, risk Medium; approval gate not triggered). The item already has a complete, measurable definition (5 ACs) and a minimal implementation sketch (`**Key Files:**`), so no feature decomposition was required — decomposition would add ceremony without reducing risk.

### Review findings

- **Requirements & AC alignment (verified against the tree):** CSV `bulletSpeed` = scout 180, diver 220, tank 150, phaser 180, swarm 180, boss 160, asteroid 100, harvester 100; `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` = 200/220/150/180/180/160/100/100; entity constants = scout 200, diver 220, tank 150, phaser 180, swarm 180, boss 160; `BaseEnemy` fallback `?? 200`. `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` = 350 (`src/core/constants.ts:160`). AC1/AC2 match exactly; ACs are consistent with the intake Appendix (Q1–Q3). No missing, contradictory or invented ACs.
- **Completeness:** `**Key Files:**` is syntactically valid (every path has a directory separator and a file extension) and every listed file exists. `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts:62` is the only pinned default expectation (`DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS.scout.bulletSpeed).toBe(200)`); `src/core/csv.test.ts:157` pins a synthetic fixture input of `200` and is unaffected.
- **Additional hard-coded sources (out of scope):** three *unknown-archetype* fallbacks also hard-code `bulletSpeed: 200` and are not covered by the Q2 enumeration (CSV + `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` + entity constants): `src/core/configStore.ts` (`genericEnemyDefault`), `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` (`resolveBaseConfig`) and `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` (`groupEnemyConfig`). Left unchanged here; tracked as a follow-up (below) so tuning cannot drift for that edge case.
- **Doc citation & divergence:** AC4 cites GDD §4.4; the enemy bullet-speed text is the blockquote in that section (line 425). The GDD currently lists enemy lifetimes that diverge from the runtime CSV (Scout 1.5 s vs CSV 1.4 s, Tank 2.0 s vs 1.5 s, Boss 2.0 s vs 0.7 s). The CSV is the runtime source of truth, so the doc's effective-range figures must be recomputed from the CSV lifetimes after halving.
- **Sequencing & dependencies:** no children or dependency edges. Test-first: write the focused halving test (AC3) before changing the values.
- **Scope sizing:** single surgical task; no decomposition needed.
- **Acceptance & testability:** each AC is pass/fail. AC3's "each archetype's … entity-constant" applies to the six archetypes that have an entity constant (scout, diver, tank, phaser, swarm, boss); asteroid and harvester have none (per the brief's own "Existing state").
- **Polish & handoff:** description is clear, well formatted and actionable.

### Follow-up

- Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks (AH-0MUX3VFUW009M539) — sibling item, `discovered-from:AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ`, non-blocking.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-06: Planning auto-completed (effort Small, risk Medium; approval gate not triggered). Verified AC numeric baselines against the tree, validated `**Key Files:**`, recorded the three out-of-scope unknown-archetype fallbacks as follow-up AH-0MUX3VFUW009M539, and noted the GDD lifetime divergence. No appendix questions were needed beyond the existing intake Q1–Q3. Marked stage `plan_complete`.

# Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns

## Problem statement

The gameplay-video capture currently uses a fixed, state-blind left/right
sweep (`scripts/capture-bot.mjs`), so captured clips show the ship wandering
rather than *playing* — and the same "player" can never become an in-game
attract/demo mode. We need a bot that **decides** what to do from the live
game state, prioritising survival over score, and that ships as an in-game
attract/demo mode which the capture tooling records.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants demo, attract and
  marketing clips that show competent gameplay without a human recording.
  - *As the maintainer, I can run `npm run capture` (or start Demo from the
    menu) and get a clip where the ship collects power-ups and minerals,
    dodges fire, and survives long enough to look like a real player.*
- **Secondary — the shipped-game player / arcade cabinet.** Wants an attract
  loop that demonstrates the game when nobody is playing.
  - *As a player leaving the menu idle, I see the game demo itself and can
    press a control to take over.*
- **Tertiary — future CI / QA.** Wants a repeatable, non-trivial gameplay
  clip for regression evidence.

## Existing state

- **State-blind bot:** `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` builds a fixed deterministic
  key plan (`buildScriptedPlan` / `BASE_SWEEP_PATTERN`); it reaches no Phaser
  internals and makes no decisions. Types live in `scripts/capture-bot.d.mts`.
- **Capture pipeline:** `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` boots headless Chromium
  (Playwright), presses Enter, holds arrow keys, records the canvas via
  `canvas.captureStream` + `MediaRecorder`, and probes the clip for
  non-triviality — from the spike **Smart capture bot... (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ)**,
  delivered under **Spike: automated gameplay video capture (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK)**.
- **Rich read-only scene state already exists** on `PlayScene`:
  `getPlayer()`, `getEnemies()`, `getEnemyBullets()`, `getDrops()`,
  `getMinerals()`, `getBoss()`, `getAliveCount()`, `getPlayerBullets()`.
- **Input seam:** `CombatCoreScene._readPlayerInput()` returns a `ControlInput`
  (`src/utils/movementModel.ts`) from held keys via `mapControlInput`; the ship
  **auto-fires**, so steering is the whole job.
- **Predictive fire signals exist:** every firing archetype has a fire
  interval and a "tell" (e.g. Scout `tryFireAimedBullet`, Diver
  `tryFireSpreadBurst`, Tank `tryFireRadialBurst`, Phaser
  `tryFireRadialBullets`), dispatched through `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`.
- **No attract/demo mode exists:** `MenuScene` offers Play Game / Settings /
  Gym Index only; `GameState` has no demo state.

## Desired change

Ship an in-game **attract/demo mode** driven by a new **survival-first bot**
whose decision logic is a pure function over a read-only game snapshot, and
wire the capture tooling to record that mode.

### Decision policy (operator spec)

Priority order, evaluated each decision tick from a read-only snapshot:

1. **Survive.** Never fly into bullets, asteroids, enemies or walls; avoid
   incoming fire.
2. **Threat response.** If a live enemy or asteroid is within the engagement
   radius, prioritise destroying/neutralising it (engage it; keep distance
   where the archetype allows).
3. **Power-ups (no nearby threat).** Seek the nearest short/medium-distance
   power-up first.
4. **Minerals.** Collect minerals that lie on the way to the chosen target,
   otherwise as a second priority after power-ups.
5. **Fire-pattern avoidance.** Read enemy fire tells/intervals and in-flight
   bullets from the snapshot and steer to avoid the anticipated shot
   (best-effort — see Q3).

### Approach (confirmed by operator)

- **Q1 = A:** the bot consumes a **read-only snapshot** built from the
  existing `PlayScene` getters. The decision logic stays pure, typed and
  unit-testable without a browser; the scene adapts the snapshot to input.
- **Q2 = C:** the bot **ships in-game** as an attract/demo mode (not
  capture-only tooling).
- **Q3 = A:** **best-effort** anticipation using the existing tell/interval
  cues plus in-flight-bullet prediction; full per-archetype pattern learning
  is out of scope (record as follow-up).

### How the two answers combine

Because the bot now ships (Q2=C), its decision module lives in `src/` and
reads live scene state directly through the read-only snapshot interface
(Q1=A). The former spike constraint "never touch `src/`" is therefore
**deliberately superseded** for this item. The capture tooling changes from
*synthesising a key plan* to *starting the in-game demo and recording it*;
the existing scripted plan remains a fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A **shipped in-game attract/demo mode** exists: it can be started from the
   main menu (and/or auto-starts after menu idle) and the bot plays a run
   autonomously; when the run ends it returns to the menu / restarts the demo
   without further human input.
2. **Survival-first priority is observable and tested.** Given a read-only
   snapshot, the bot: (a) ignores distant targets while a power-up is in
   short/medium range; (b) prioritises engaging a live enemy/asteroid once it
   is within the engagement radius; (c) treats minerals as on-the-way or
   second-priority pickups. Each branch is covered by a deterministic unit
   test.
3. **Fire-pattern avoidance demonstrably reduces avoidable hits.** Against a
   scripted tell/interval fire pattern, the bot takes fewer avoidable hits
   than a reactive-only (bullet-only) baseline, and steers away from an
   anticipated shot before it is fired. Verified by a deterministic test with
   a stubbed firing enemy.
4. **The bot never suicides:** over a deterministic simulated run it does not
   deliberately collide with a bullet, asteroid, enemy or wall when a safe
   alternative exists (asserted by unit tests over the pure decision
   function).
5. **Capture records the in-game demo and stays non-trivial:** `npm run
   capture` can record the attract/demo mode and still produces a clip that
   passes the video+audio non-triviality gate, exiting non-zero on a
   trivial/silent clip.
6. **Normal play is unaffected:** starting Play Game and running
   `npm test` / `npm run build` behave exactly as before; demo behaviour is
   opt-in and cannot leak into a normal session.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** any shared gameplay behaviour the bot relies on must
  stay in `src/scenes/core/` and be exercised by both the gyms and
  `PlayScene`; no divergent copies. If the bot is `PlayScene`-only, record
  that clearly.
- **Determinism & testability:** decision logic must be a pure function over
  a snapshot so it is unit-testable under vitest (canvas is stubbed in
  `src/test/setup.ts`); avoid wall-clock dependence inside the decision.
- **No new heavy dependencies** for the shipped path; capture keeps its
  opt-in Playwright dependency.
- **Do not edit** `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent
  infrastructure.
- **Tunables** (engagement radius, power-up/mineral ranges, danger margins)
  live in one shared place, not scattered magic numbers.
- Out of scope (record as linked follow-ups): full per-archetype fire-pattern
  learning; seeding all RNG for frame-reproducible runs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/` (new) — bot decision module: `BotSnapshot` type,
  `decideBotInput(snapshot)` pure function, threat/collect/avoid policy,
  tunables. Unit tests alongside.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build the snapshot from existing getters; drive
  the shared input path with bot input in demo mode; demo lifecycle
  (start/stop, return to menu); expose a demo-mode flag for tests.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — attract/demo entry point (menu option and/or
  idle-attract timer) and "press to take over".
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — seam so the scene can consume bot
  input instead of (or alongside) keyboard input in `_readPlayerInput()`.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — demo/session mode flag if the run is
  session-scoped.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register/wire any new scene or demo entry.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — start and
  record the in-game demo; retain the scripted plan as fallback.
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — `ControlInput` the bot produces.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`, `src/entities/Scout.ts`, `src/entities/Diver.ts`,
  `src/entities/Tank.ts`, `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — fire tell/interval
  signals the bot predicts from.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts`, `src/entities/Mineral.ts`,
  `src/powerups/` — targets and hazards the snapshot exposes.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — capture now records the in-game demo.
- `README.md`, GDD / menu docs — document attract/demo mode.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — parity updates only if shared behaviour changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — attract trigger:** the demo is reachable from the main menu
  and auto-runs after menu idle; the operator may narrow this to menu-only or
  idle-only during review.
- **Assumption — superseding the spike boundary:** Q2=C authorises editing
  `src/` and the shipped bundle; this is recorded here because the capture
  spike explicitly avoided it.
- **Risk — false confidence in dodging:** best-effort prediction can still be
  hit; the AC asserts *fewer avoidable hits than baseline*, not
  invulnerability.
- **Risk — shipped-mode regressions:** a demo mode touching input/scene
  lifecycle could affect normal play; mitigation is an opt-in flag plus
  regression tests (AC6).
- **Risk — canvas-stubbed test env:** the bot cannot be exercised through the
  real renderer in vitest; mitigation is a pure decision function plus the
  opt-in capture job.
- **Risk — scope creep (explicit):** per-archetype pattern learning, RNG
  seeding, and CI wiring are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless
  browser + scripted bot); the tooling and its design boundary this item
  supersedes.
- **AH-0MUWTNPYJ0031FQE** — capture audio; the non-trivial clip gate the
  capture AC reuses.
- **AH-0MUWYQQYU001G6OG**, **AH-0MUWYQRAS0054VO5**, **AH-0MUWYQQMZ007QIQZ** —
  capture audio tap / probe helpers.
- **AH-0MUII3CXX0023H24** — Shared power-up drop layer (spawner, lifecycle,
  collection, magnet, cues): the drops the bot seeks.
- **AH-0MUTPEJNO002V2NA**, **AH-0MUTPEJZL008LGDP** — Shared mineral scoop
  helper / PlayScene wiring: the minerals the bot seeks.
- **AH-0MU8QTS7O006DSAE**, **AH-0MUUM1167006CXAK** — P9 Magnet attraction:
  affects whether the bot should chase drops/minerals or let them come.

# Re-calibrate L4-L5 Generated Campaign Targets After Enemy Bullet-Speed Halving

## Problem statement

Halving every enemy `bulletSpeed` (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ) lowered each firing archetype's `enemyDifficulty` score by ~0.5–1 point (weight 5/116). The difficulty sequencer's `argmin` now selects degenerate L4–L5 wave compositions — single-enemy firing waves — diverging from hand-tuned targets.

## Users

- **Player** — wants playable, escalating L4–L5 challenge, not trivial single-enemy waves.
- **Game designer** — wants the sequencer to track hand-tuned targets without re-balancing weights.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want L4–L5 campaign waves to present a meaningful, varied challenge, not degenerate single-enemy encounters.
- As a **game designer**, I want the sequencer's generated compositions to stay close to hand-tuned targets without re-tuning enemyDifficulty weights.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Non-degenerate compositions.** No L4–L5 generated wave consists of a single firing enemy. Compositions differ per wave (verified by enemyKey:count).
- **AC2 — Tight band to targets.** Each L4–L5 generated wave's measured `waveDifficulty` is within ±1.0 of its `targetDifficulty`. (Proposed resolution: the original "agreed band" is set to ±1.0, tighter than the existing per-wave CSV tolerance (~2.0), to prevent noticeable drift while allowing valid compositions.)
- **AC3 — No regression to base values.** `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed`, `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`, and every enemy `bulletSpeed` remain at the halved values from AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ.
- **AC4 — Full suite passes.** All tests pass, including new regression tests asserting AC1/AC2 and updated existing regression tests.

## Constraints

- Do not change `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed`, `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`, or enemy `bulletSpeed` values.
- No divergent copies between gym and game scenes.
- Minimal change: re-derive `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` or enhance `sequenceVariedWaves` — not both.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` (`src/core/configStore.ts`): L4 = [16, 24, 28], L5 = [45, 62].
- `difficulty-curves.csv` has mirrored L4–L5 targets.
- After halving: L4 waves changed from `scoutx18 / diverx18 / tankx18` (measured 22.9/31.3/36.2) to `swarmx1 / tankx1 / phaserx1` (measured 1.8/2.8/3.0).
- L5 w1: `phaserx12+scoutx18` (measured 41.1) → `phaserx12+swarmx1` (measured 29.1).
- Per-wave CSV tolerance is ~2.0 — the shift is within tolerance but composition quality is poor.

## Desired change

Re-derive L4–L5 `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` and `difficulty-curves.csv` rows against **post-halving** `enemyDifficulty` scores so `argmin` selects the same high-quality compositions. If target re-tuning alone is insufficient, enhance `sequenceVariedWaves` to prefer distinct archetypes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — Update `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` for L4/L5.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — Update mirrored L4–L5 targets.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — `sequenceVariedWaves` (if enhanced approach needed).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — New regression: L4–L5 `waveDifficulty` within ±1.0 of target; non-degenerate composition check.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` — Gym-parity regression for AC1/AC2.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — Read-only: inspect post-halving archetype scores.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep (low).** Re-tuning difficulty weights or reverting bullet-speed halving is documented as out of scope (parent Q3-A).
- **Approach uncertainty (medium).** Re-deriving targets may not fully restore quality if score ordering fundamentally changed; `sequenceVariedWaves` enhancement is the fallback, with more risk.
- **Regression-test churn (low).** Updating targets in `configStore.ts` and `difficulty-curves.csv` will require re-baselining existing pinned tests.
- **Assumption.** Re-deriving targets against post-halving scores is the preferred approach.
- **Assumption.** A ±1.0 difficulty-point tolerance is appropriate.

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent; completed).
- AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign (completed; prior retuning).
- AH-0MUQ5262M009UFLU — Implement dynamic, varied non-firing opening waves (completed; `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` precedent).

# Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item TEMPORARILY, not permanently

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Stage:** intake_complete

## Problem statement

Every collection currently increments a **run-scoped, permanent** level for the
item, regardless of where it came from. A field pickup and a hold-full
(mineral-choice) reward both call the same permanent mutation path:

- Power-ups — `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, permanent)` → `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`).
- Weapons — `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` unconditionally does
  `this._weaponLevels.set(weaponId, this.getWeaponLevel(weaponId) + 1)`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).

Consequently a field pickup permanently raises the level, and the level
persists after the timed effect expires. This is wrong: field pickups are
**temporary** improvements; only hold-full (mineral-choice) rewards are
**permanent**. Because the hold-full choice reads `getWeaponLevels()` /
`getPowerUpLevels()`, a temporary field pickup also currently inflates the
level offered by the next hold-full choice, which compounds the bug.

## Users and user story

> As the player, when I collect a power-up or weapon in the field I want its
> level to improve **only for the duration of the pickup's timed effect**, so
> that when the timer expires the item drops back to the level it had
> permanently earned. Permanent level improvements should come **only** from
> hold-full (mineral-choice) rewards.

Stakeholders: the player (correct, predictable power growth) and the producer /
balance owner (the hold-full choice must price the *permanent* level only).

## Required behaviour (worked examples)

Let `permanentGrants` = number of hold-full rewards taken for the item, and
`tempStacks` = number of field pickups collected during the current timed
window.

- An item is **owned/active** while `permanentGrants + tempStacks >= 1`.
- `permanentUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants - 1` (first hold-full reward = base
  level 0; each further hold-full reward = +1), i.e. lvl0 is the base tier.
- `effectiveLevel = permanentUpgradeLevel + tempStacks` when owned.
- A field pickup: `tempStacks += 1` **and** (re)starts the item's timed window
  (weapons `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` = 10 s; power-ups their existing timed duration,
  e.g. P3 shield 15 s). The window refreshes on each new field pickup.
- On window expiry: `tempStacks = 0`; `effectiveLevel` reverts to
  `permanentUpgradeLevel`. If `permanentGrants == 0` the item becomes inactive
  (no permanent level). Unconsumed consumable grants persist (see Resolved
  decisions 1).
- A hold-full reward: increments `permanentGrants` permanently, no timeout, and
  does **not** touch `tempStacks`.

Worked examples:

**A — field pickups only (no hold-full reward)**
1. Pick up P3 → lvl0 for x s.
2. Pick up P3 again before x s → lvl1 for x s (window refreshed).
3. x s expires → back to lvl0 / effect gone (no permanent level retained).

**B — hold-full reward then field pickups**
1. Take P3 from a hold-full choice → lvl0, permanent, no timeout.
2. Pick up P3 in the field → lvl1 for x s.
3. x s expires → back to lvl0 (permanent).
4. Take P3 from another hold-full choice → lvl1, permanent.

## Resolved decisions

1. **Unconsumed consumable grants on expiry (P6 Phase Shift charges / P7
   Teleport stacks).** Resolved: **(b) persist until consumed.** Expiry of the
   temporary window must **not** remove charges/teleports already granted; the
   player keeps them until used. The permanent/temporary level distinction
   still governs the *level* (and therefore future grants), but does not claw
   back an already-granted consumable. The producer asked us to *consider
   creating a second power-up type* for this consumable-grant distinction;
   that exploration is tracked as a non-blocking follow-up,
   [Consider a distinct power-up type for consumable temporary grants (P6/P7) (AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN)].
2. **`★ New` badge for a field-only item.** Resolved: **(a) permanent grants
   only.** Ownership for the hold-full choice derives from `permanentGrants`,
   so an item only ever picked up in the field still reads `★ New` until
   permanently acquired, and the choice never offers a level-up on a level
   that vanishes on expiry.
3. **Exact temporary window per weapon/power-up.** Resolved: **(a) reuse
   existing timed-effect durations** — weapons `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s),
   power-ups their configured duration (e.g. P3 shield 15 s), refreshed on each
   new field pickup. No new balance constants.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — **Field pickups are temporary.** Collecting a power-up or weapon in the
  field raises the item's effective level by one only for the item's timed
  window and starts/refreshes that window. When the window expires, the
  temporary level is removed and the effective level reverts to the permanent
  level (or the item becomes inactive when there is no permanent level).
- AC2 — **Hold-full rewards are permanent.** Applying a `weapon-level` /
  `power-up-level` choice (and a first-time `weapon` / `powerup` choice)
  permanently raises the item's level with no timeout, independent of any
  active temporary window.
- AC3 — **Worked examples reproduce exactly.** Both example sequences (A and B)
  produce the states described above; tests assert the effective level and
  active/inactive state at each step.
- AC4 — **The hold-full choice reflects the permanent level only.** The
  `ChoiceContext` supplied by every launcher (`PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeaponLeveling`) reports each item's **permanent**
  level, so a temporary field pickup never inflates the level-up offered (no
  offering "Lv.2" when only "Lv.1" is permanent). The change summary and
  `★ New` badge likewise derive from permanent level (ownership = permanent
  grants; Resolved decision 2).
- AC5 — **HUD/readouts show the effective level.** Any level readout (HUD
  weapon level, gym panels) shows `permanent + temporary` and updates when a
  temporary window expires.
- AC6 — **Run restart clears everything.** `reset()` / `resetWeaponLevels()` /
  `resetPowerUpLevels()` clear both permanent and temporary level state.
- AC7 — **Single source of truth.** The permanent/temporary distinction lives
  once (in `PowerUpLevelStore` for power-ups and in the `Player` weapon-level
  state), consumed identically by the game and every gym. No second,
  divergent copy of the level maths is added.
- AC8 — **Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; the existing parity/equivalence
  guards continue to pass. Update the gym scenes in the same change per the
  repo gym↔game parity convention.
- AC9 — **Existing effect semantics preserved for hybrids and consumables.**
  - P9 Magnet / P10 Mineral Scoop remain hybrid: a field pickup is a
    refresh-only timed attraction (now with a temporary level); a hold-full
    reward is a permanent stack. The permanent stack count derives from
    `permanentGrants` and is unaffected by temporary levels.
  - P6 Phase Shift charges / P7 Teleport stacks keep their existing
    grant-then-consume semantics. Per Resolved decision 1, unconsumed grants
    from a temporary field pickup **persist until consumed** and are **not**
    removed when the window expires; tests assert that expiry removes the
    temporary *level* but leaves stored charges/teleports intact.
- AC10 — **Testing and validation.** Unit tests cover the worked examples, the
  temporary/permanent split, expiry revert, hold-full permanence, choice
  context, HUD readout and run reset. Full project test suite must pass with
  the new changes.
- AC11 — **Documentation updated.** GDD §4.4.2/§4.4.3 and the module doc
  comments (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`,
  `src/entities/Player.ts`) describe the temporary/permanent split, including
  the consumable-grant persistence rule. All related documentation is updated
  to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant
  wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Preserve the single mutation-point architecture (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K): the
  split is introduced **inside** `PowerUpLevelStore` and the `Player`
  weapon-level state, not in a parallel counter.
- No new balance constants: reuse `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` and existing per-power-up
  durations (Resolved decision 3).
- Preserve P9/P10 hybrid semantics and P6/P7 consumable semantics (AC9).
- Keep gym↔game parity; gyms and `PlayScene` run the same code (AC8).
- Do not scope-creep into the "distinct power-up type" redesign; that is the
  separate follow-up item AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN.

## Existing state

- `PowerUpLevelStore` tracks a single run-scoped `level` per power-up plus a
  separate `_permanentGrants` map; `collect()` always increments `level`,
  and only `permanent=true` also increments `_permanentGrants`. There is no
  temporary-vs-permanent split of `level`, and the "level persists across a
  timed effect expiring" contract is documented in the module header.
- `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` always increments `_weaponLevels`; the
  `permanent` flag only controls whether the weapon is added to
  `_permanentWeapons` vs `_weaponTimers`. `_weaponTimers` expiry deletes the
  timer but never touches `_weaponLevels`.
- The hold-full choice consumes `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` /
  the store's `getLevels()`, so temporary field pickups currently inflate the
  offered level.

## Desired change

Split each item's level into a **permanent** component (hold-full grants only)
and a **temporary** component (field pickups, tied to the existing timed
window). Expose an effective level (`permanent + temporary`) for readouts and
the effect path, and a permanent level for the hold-full choice. Remove the
temporary component when the item's timed window expires (without clawing back
already-granted consumables). Clear both on run reset.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — consumable banking (Resolved decision 1b).** Persisting unconsumed
  temporary grants lets a player bank charges/teleports across an expiry.
  Mitigation: only the *level* reverts, so repeat field pickups still stop
  granting at the temporary cap once consumed; consumption remains bounded by
  play. Accepted by the producer at intake.
- **Risk — extra state complexity.** Tracking `tempStacks` per item alongside
  the timed effects risks a second, divergent counter. Mitigation: the split
  lives once, inside `PowerUpLevelStore` / `Player` (AC7), with no parallel
  counter.
- **Risk — gym↔game divergence.** A temp/permanent fix applied to only one
  caller would break parity. Mitigation: shared core plus the existing
  parity/equivalence guards (AC8).
- **Scope-creep risk.** The producer's "second power-up type" idea could pull
  this fix into a redesign. Mitigation: recorded as non-blocking follow-up
  AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN; explicitly out of scope here (Constraints).
- **Assumption.** `permanentUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants - 1` matches the
  existing level semantics (first grant = base level 0; each further grant
  = +1), mirroring `resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`.
- **Assumption.** The temporary window reuses the existing configured
  durations (`WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 s; per-power-up durations) with no new
  tuning constants.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Needs the `PowerUpLevelStore` split:
  permanent grants vs temporary field-pickup stacks; expose effective vs
  permanent levels; `collect(id, permanent)` routes the field pickup to the
  temporary component.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Needs the timed-effect lifecycle
  (`_startOrRefreshTimed`/expiry, `P9_MAGNET_DURATION`, `P10_SCOOP_DURATION`)
  to clear the temporary level on expiry, while leaving stored P6/P7 grants
  intact.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Needs `equipWeapon` / `_weaponTimers` /
  `getWeaponLevel` / `getWeaponLevels` to split temporary from permanent; only
  `equipWeapon(id, true)` raises the permanent level; the 10 s timeout expiry
  clears the temporary level.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — Needs `ChoiceContext` / `buildChoiceCandidates`
  to consume the **permanent** level and derive `★ New` ownership from
  permanent grants.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — Need to supply the permanent-level
  context and keep parity.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Needs the effective-level readout.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Needs §4.4.2 / §4.4.3 updated to describe
  the temporary/permanent split and consumable-grant persistence.

## Related work

## Summary

Found during post-epic verification of Smart capture bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ). The new default in-game-demo capture path (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V) is **flaky**: roughly 2 in 3 runs produce a trivial (static, silent) clip because the demo never starts.

## Root cause

`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` starts the demo by pressing **Tab** (focuses the menu's Watch Demo control) then **Enter** (activates it) with no delay between them. The FocusManager processes both keydowns, but dispatching them back-to-back races the focus change. Reproduction (3 runs each):

- immediate Tab+Enter: 1/3 produced motion
- Tab, 300 ms, Enter: 3/3 produced motion
- 1 s settle then Tab+Enter: 1/3 produced motion
- pointer click on Watch Demo: 3/3 produced motion

When the keys are pressed before the focus change lands, neither the demo nor a normal run starts; the capture records the static menu. The audio tap still reports 1 track (it mirrors the master-gain connection regardless of context state), so the failure looks like "audio ready" but the clip is silent and static.

## Desired behaviour

The capture's demo-start path must reliably start the demo (and the scripted path must reliably start Play Game).

## Fix

Dispatch the start keys with a short inter-key gap (e.g. 250 ms) instead of back-to-back. Encode the timing in a pure, testable `captureStartPlan(mode, gapMs)` helper (each entry `{ key, delayAfterMs }`), consumed by `runCapture`. Keep the single-key scripted path unchanged in effect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The capture start sequence waits a documented gap between the Tab and Enter keys; a pure helper encodes the per-key delay and is unit-tested.
- AC2: Repeated end-to-end demo captures (3 in a row) are all non-trivial (non-static, non-silent).
- AC3: The scripted fallback still starts Play Game and produces a non-trivial clip.
- AC4: Full suite, typecheck and build pass.

# Demo-mode game-over dwell

## Summary

In demo/attract mode the run currently returns straight to the menu on game
over (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY AC5 — non-scoring). For a full-run capture tail to
show the outcome, the demo must hold on a game-over screen for a configurable
dwell of at least the capture tail before returning to the menu
(parent AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU, AC4).

**User story:** As a viewer of a captured full run, I see the VICTORY/DEFEAT
screen for at least 5 s after the run ends before the demo loops back to the
menu; as a normal player, my game is unchanged and the demo still never writes
to the leaderboard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** In demo mode, game over shows the game-over screen (VICTORY /
  DEFEAT + final score) and holds for `DEMO_GAME_OVER_DWELL_MS` (default
  `>= 5000`, single-source constant) before returning to the menu.
- **AC2:** The demo remains **non-scoring**: it never qualifies for, enters or
  persists a leaderboard score, and never accepts initials.
- **AC3:** Non-demo play is byte-for-byte unchanged: a normal run still
  transitions to the normal interactive `GameOverScene` exactly as before.
- **AC4:** The dwell is configurable and driven by the pure dwell helper from
  the foundation child; an override lets tests run with a short/zero dwell.
- **AC5:** Unit/integration tests cover: dwell duration honoured in demo mode,
  return-to-menu after the dwell, no leaderboard write in demo mode, and
  normal-mode `GameOverScene` unaffected.
- **AC6:** `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

Recommended: start `GameOverScene` from demo `_finishRun` with a demo flag
(`{ won, score, demo: true }`), render the outcome but skip leaderboard
qualification/initials, and schedule the return to `MenuScene` after the dwell.
Alternative (recorded as an OPEN QUESTION): hold an outcome overlay in
`PlayScene` for the dwell. Either way the decision is the pure dwell helper.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — demo `_finishRun` dwell path
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — demo-safe outcome rendering (no scoring)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — tests

## Dependencies

Depends on **Run-end signal, tail and dwell helpers** (dwell decision).

## Deliverables

Configurable, non-scoring demo game-over dwell with tests.

# Intake Brief — Enhance Central AI boss encounter

**Work item:** Enhance Central AI boss encounter: 200 HP, more minions, figure-8 movement, top-screen health bar, hit feedback (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X)

## Problem statement

The Central AI boss encounter is currently a static, 400-hit grind: the boss does not move, the health bar is drawn relative to the boss container (so it is visibly displaced rather than at the top of the screen), and individual hits give no feedback beyond a bullet disappearing. Players cannot read their progress and the fight lacks the mobility and impact expected of a climactic boss. This work item reduces the boss's total health to **200**, reinforces the fight with **more minions**, gives the boss **figure-of-8 movement**, fixes the **health bar to the top of the screen**, and makes **every hit obvious through SFX and VFX**.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** fights the boss after clearing Level 5 and wants a readable, impactful, mobile encounter.
  - *As a player, I want to see the boss's health decrease with every hit so I know my shots are registering.*
  - *As a player, I want the fight to feel dynamic and dangerous, with the boss moving and more enemies on screen.*
  - *As a player, I want clear audio/visual feedback on each hit so the encounter feels responsive.*
- **Developer/maintainer (secondary):** wants the change implemented once in the shared core so the game and boss gyms stay in parity.
  - *As a developer, I want the boss behaviour to live in the shared core so `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
2. **More minions are spawned with the boss.** Phase 1 spawns **12 scouts** (6 per side), phase 2 spawns **12 divers** (6 per side), phase 3 remains **0** (the pulse is the threat), and phase 4 spawns **15 swarm**. Verified by `BossMinions` unit tests asserting the per-phase counts via `minionCountForPhase`.
3. **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.
4. **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
5. **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
6. **Test coverage.** New/updated tests cover the health model, minion counts, figure-8 motion, health-bar placement, and hit feedback across `Boss.test.ts`, `BossMinions.test.ts`, `GymBoss.test.ts`, `PlayScene.test.ts`, and the audio cue contract.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the Game Design Document (§4.3), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1 parity), and the audio cue mapping/manifest.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (mandatory):** gameplay behaviour must live in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/entities/`) and be consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss`; no divergent copies. The `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must still pass.
- **Preserve the 4-phase model:** do not change the phase attack patterns, telegraphs, or reward gating; only retune totals/counts and add movement/feedback.
- **Health bar model:** keep the existing proportional `getHpFraction()` fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
- **Audio pipeline:** a new SFX cue must be registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` and `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` (the contract test enforces completeness).
- **No new dependencies.**
- Stay within the existing visual/neon style and UK-English documentation conventions.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: 4 phases × `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` = **400 total hits**; `applyFormationPosition()` is a static `setPosition(baseX, baseY)`; `healthBarGraphics` is added as a **child of the boss container** but drawn with screen coordinates (so it renders offset by the boss position); `takeDamage()` only plays the phase-transition cue on a depleting hit; no per-hit feedback.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts`: phase 1 = 8 scouts (4+4), phase 2 = 8 divers (4+4), phase 3 = 0, phase 4 = 10 swarm.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_damageBoss()`: applies damage and awards score/summons minions on phase depletion; no hit SFX/VFX.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` `damageBoss()`: gym equivalent, mirrors the game's gating.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_advanceBoss()`: shared per-frame boss advance consumed by both the game and the gym (the correct place for shared movement/feedback).
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`: reusable `spawnBulletImpact()` flash already used for non-lethal hits on multi-hit enemies (Harvester) but **not** wired to the boss.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`: no boss-hit cue exists.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.3 documents the 400-hit model and static boss.

## Desired change

1. Retune boss health to a **200-hit total** (4 phases × 50) and update the constants/comments/tests.
2. Increase minion counts to **P1 = 12, P2 = 12, P3 = 0, P4 = 15**.
3. Add **figure-8 (lemniscate) movement** around the spawn anchor in the shared boss core, with parameters ≈120 px / ≈60 px / ≈8 s, bounded to the playfield.
4. **Re-parent the health bar** out of the boss container so it is camera-fixed at the top-centre of the screen, always visible, and unaffected by boss movement; keep the proportional fill and phase dividers.
5. Add a **dedicated boss-hit SFX cue** and an **obvious hit VFX** (impact flash/burst at the hit point) applied on every hit through a shared path used by both the game and the gym; keep the existing phase-transition feedback.
6. Update tests and documentation (GDD, enemy design/parity doc, audio mapping).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — health constants (50/phase, 200 total), figure-8 movement, health-bar re-parenting/positioning, per-hit feedback hook.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` — increased per-phase minion counts.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared boss movement/feedback seam for parity.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring; health-bar layering.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — `damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring (parity).
- `src/audio/effects.ts`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — new boss-hit cue and mapping.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — reusable/extended impact flash for boss hits.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/waves/BossMinions.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed) — established the `phaseAdvanced`-gated score/minion behaviour this work preserves.
- **AH-0MUUJCL8J00632T7** – Boss.ts per-phase HP model, return contract, health-bar fill (completed) — the `getHpFraction()` proportional fill this work keeps.
- **AH-0MUTV3J7T006MZ4K** – Increase Central AI boss hits-per-phase 10x (completed) — prior health tuning precedent.
- **AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE** – Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (completed) — gym that must stay in parity.
- **AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ** – Integrate boss encounter into PlayScene (completed) — boss spawn wiring and minion sums.
- **AH-0MUD9R3ZC0006M4I** – Extract collision core and host bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback (completed) — shared impact-feedback precedent.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed)
- **AH-0MU3X86GT001YM5D** – Identify enemy refactor opportunities (completed)
- **AH-0MUUJFOTM009ORQM** – GDD and code comment documentation updates (AC7) (completed)

Repository file matches: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "200 health" means 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each), not 200 per phase.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** minion increase ≈50% in phases 1, 2 and 4; phase 3 stays minion-free.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** figure-8 defaults 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s; boss-only motion; top-centre screen-fixed health bar; new per-hit SFX + impact-flash VFX.
- **Risk:** figure-8 motion could push the boss off-screen or desync aimed shots/minions — mitigate with bounded amplitude and using the boss's live position for aiming/collision.
- **Risk:** health-bar re-parenting may break tests that assume the bar is a container child — update those tests and add explicit screen-position assertions.
- **Risk:** the new SFX may need a ToneForge recipe/baked asset; if a new recipe is required the audio build pipeline must render it (or reuse an existing recipe) and the manifest must stay complete so the contract test passes.
- **Risk:** gameplay change requires parity across `PlayScene` and all boss gyms — implement in shared core only; verify with the equivalence/parity tests.
- **Scope-creep:** further boss rebalancing (attack patterns, telegraph timings, additional phases) is out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What does "reduce the health to 200" mean?** Options: (a) 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each); (b) 200 per phase (800 total); (c) other. **Recommended:** (a) — preserves the 4-phase model.
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2: How much should the minion count increase, and in which phases?** Options: (a) ~50% more in phases 1, 2 and 4 (P1 12, P2 12, P3 0, P4 15); (b) roughly double all; (c) add minions to phase 3; (d) other. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3: Are the implementation defaults acceptable?** (figure-8: 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s, boss-only; hit feedback: new hit SFX + impact flash on every hit, keeping phase-transition feedback; health bar: screen-fixed top-centre). **Recommended:** accept.
  - **Answer (operator):** "yes". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when offered a hold-full choice I want a reasonable chance of upgrading an upgradeable weapon or power-up I already own, so my build keeps improving rather than forcing me to chase new items."
- **Designer:** "As a designer, I want owned upgrades to appear 10% more often so progression feels steady across runs."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 10% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (weapon-level and power-up-level) have a 1.1× weight multiplier applied during candidate selection. Unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0× weight.
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The weighting logic lives in `buildChoiceCandidates` or the strategy layer; no duplicate weighting code in scenes or gyms.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`.
- **AC4 — Configurable weight.** The 1.1× multiplier is a named constant (e.g. `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1`) so it can be tuned later without hunting for magic numbers.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests verify: (a) owned-level candidates receive 1.1× weight; (b) weighted random selection produces the expected distribution (statistically, over many trials, owned items appear ~10% more often than unowned items relative to pool size); (c) gym↔game parity tests pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once and be consumed by both the game and every gym.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy` interface or existing `ChoiceOption` consumers.
- **No gameplay logic changes beyond weighting:** the candidate list itself is unchanged — only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add weighting logic in `buildChoiceCandidates` or `createRandomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — no changes expected (they already pass context).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — new tests for weighted selection.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — parity tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed).
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Statistical testing (low):** proving 10% bias requires many trials; tests should use a large sample size (e.g. 10,000 draws) and a reasonable tolerance band.
- **Assumption:** "10% more likely" means a 1.1× multiplicative weight, not an additive 10 percentage points.
- **Assumption:** "owned upgrade" means `weapon-level` and `power-up-level` kind options in the candidate list.

# Bot still controls the player after Watch Demo then Play Game

## Problem statement

After the player selects **Watch Demo** on the main menu, every subsequent
**Play Game** start can inherit the demo's scene data, so the bot keeps
driving the ship instead of the keyboard. This is a critical, player-visible
control bug: the player cannot actually play a normal run until the page is
reloaded.

## Users

- **Player** — selects Watch Demo, then Play Game, and expects full keyboard
  control in the new run.
  - *As a player, after watching the demo I want Play Game to hand me full
    keyboard control so I can play a normal run.*
  - *As a player, taking over the demo with a key and later starting a fresh
    game must not leave the bot steering my ship.*

## Root cause (verified against the pinned Phaser source)

Phaser's `Systems.start(data)` only assigns `settings.data` when `data` is
truthy:

```js
// node_modules/phaser/src/scene/Systems.js
start: function (data) {
    if (data) { settings.data = data; }
    ...
}
```

`SceneManager.start(key, data)` forwards `data` as-is, and
`SceneManager` invokes `scene.init.call(scene, settings.data)`. Because this
scene instance is reused:

1. **Watch Demo** → `MenuScene.startDemo()` calls
   `this.scene.start('PlayScene', { demo: true })` → `settings.data` becomes
   `{ demo: true }` and `PlayScene.init()` sets `demoMode = true`.
2. The demo ends (or the player takes over with a key). PlayScene shuts down
   (its `settings.data` is **not** cleared).
3. **Play Game** → `this.scene.start('PlayScene')` passes **no data**, so
   `Systems.start(undefined)` leaves the stale `{ demo: true }` in place;
   `PlayScene.init()` reads it again and re-enables demo mode, and
   `getBotInput()` therefore returns the bot decision instead of `null`.

Both normal Play Game entry points are affected (pointer handler and the
`FocusManager` keyboard activation) because both omit the data argument.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts:127` and `:267` start `PlayScene` with no data;
  `:316` (`startDemo`) starts it with `{ demo: true }`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:474` `init(data)` sets
  `this.demoMode = data?.demo === true`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1405` `getBotInput()` returns the governed bot
  input only while `demoMode` is true.
- Existing tests only assert normal start is non-demo on a **fresh boot**
  (`PlayScene.test.ts` "AC6 — demo mode is false when started normally"), so
  the stale-data path is untested.

## Desired change

A normal Play Game start (and any non-demo restart) must always run with the
bot disabled, regardless of whether a demo ran earlier in the same session.
The fix must be explicit rather than relying on Phaser's data-clearing
behaviour, so a future scene start that omits data cannot silently re-enter
demo mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No bot after demo then Play Game.** With the game booted, start
  the demo (`MenuScene.startDemo()`), let the demo scene shut down (or take
  over), then start a normal game via the Play Game path and assert
  `PlayScene.isDemoMode() === false` and `getBotInput() === null`; the ship
  responds to keyboard input, not the bot.
- [ ] **AC2 — Explicit data on every normal start.** Both normal Play Game
  entry points in `MenuScene` pass an explicit non-demo payload
  (e.g. `{ demo: false }`), and a regression test proves a normal start after
  a demo does not inherit `{ demo: true }` from Phaser's reused
  `settings.data`.
- [ ] **AC3 — PlayScene is fail-safe.** `PlayScene.init()` treats absent,
  `undefined`, or non-`true` data as non-demo, and the scene-start contract is
  documented in the `init()`/`startDemo()` comments so a future caller cannot
  omit the flag and accidentally re-enter demo mode.
- [ ] **AC4 — Gym↔game parity preserved.** The fix touches only the
  game/gym-shared demo-input seam; the shared
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity
  docs assertion still pass, and no gym gains divergent demo handling.
- [ ] **AC5 — Automated regression test.** At least one automated test
  reproduces the exact sequence (Watch Demo → return to menu/take-over →
  normal Play Game) and fails on the pre-fix code; it lives at the
  MenuScene↔PlayScene integration boundary.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the gym↔game parity convention in `AGENTS.md`: share demo-input
  behaviour via `src/scenes/core/`; no divergent copies.
- Do not change demo/attract behaviour itself (start, take-over, non-scoring
  end-of-run, idle timer) — only the data-handling that leaks demo mode into
  normal play.
- Keep the fix minimal and local to the scene-start data path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** reproduction requires only the same page session (Phaser
  reuses the scene instance); no persistence is involved.
- **Risk:** other `scene.start('PlayScene')` call sites (present or future)
  could re-introduce the leak — mitigated by AC2 (explicit payloads) and AC3
  (fail-safe `init`) plus the regression test.
- **Risk:** changing the normal-start payload could affect tests that assert
  `init()` receives no data — covered by running the full suite (AC7).
- **Scope creep:** unrelated demo-mode polish (reaction time, capture tooling)
  is out of scope; record any such finds as separate linked work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — pass explicit `{ demo: false }` on both normal
  Play Game starts (pointer handler + `FocusManager` activation).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — harden `init()` against absent/stale data and
  document the start-data contract.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — assert the normal Play Game payload.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — end-to-end regression test for
  Watch Demo → Play Game.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — restart-after-demo regression coverage.
- `docs/` demo/attract documentation — note the explicit start-data contract.

## Related work

See the automated report below, plus the parent demo-mode work items:
Attract/demo entry point in MenuScene (AH-0MUX4966Z0009P9Q), Demo mode engine:
input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY), Demo-mode
integration and regression verification (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P), and Demo bot:
human-like input limits (AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was not interview-driven: the operator supplied the reproduction,
the root cause was verified against the pinned Phaser source, and the operator
set the priority (`critical`). No open questions remain.

- Q: "Where exactly does the demo leak into a normal run?" — Answer
  (agent, verified): Phaser's `Systems.start(data)` only writes
  `settings.data` for truthy data, so a no-argument
  `scene.start('PlayScene')` after `{ demo: true }` reuses the stale payload.
  Source: `node_modules/phaser/src/scene/Systems.js:740-744`,
  `SceneManager.js:1255-1262`, `MenuScene.ts:127,267,316`,
  `PlayScene.ts:474,1405`.
- Assumption: the fix should be explicit at the call sites *and* fail-safe in
  `PlayScene.init()` (recorded under Acceptance Criteria AC2/AC3).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** – Feature: Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests (completed)
- **AH-0MUITRWLO001Y4Y5** – End-to-end acceptance tests for sequenced wave generation (completed)
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** – Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless browser + scripted bot) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: bot, bug, call, calls, cause (+49 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: bot, call, calls, cause, controls (+44 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: bot, call, calls, cause, controls (+38 more)
